evidence.dominant_driver: German wholesale inflation acceleration led by energy/petroleum

components.energy: petroleum products and related energy categories were key drivers

absorption.reason: DAX remained around -0.5% while the hot inflation print reinforced an existing energy/rates headwind.

evidence.decision_notes: Hot print confirms existing European inflation shock; residual downside edge is modest because DAX was already lower.

regimes.global: higher yields + expensive oil; cautious risk tone

immediate.rationale: Hotter wholesale inflation confirms the existing rates/energy headwind.

next_session.rationale: Much depends on ECB/rates and whether energy prices stay elevated.

15m.rationale: Confirmed risk-off context leaves modest residual downside.

1h.rationale: Hot input-price inflation can keep bund/rate pressure elevated.

4h.rationale: The index is already lower and the shock may be increasingly absorbed.

next_session.rationale: ECB and energy follow-through matter more than the single print.

predictions.counter_case: If oil and European yields retreat, the already-weaker DAX could rebound despite the hot wholesale print.

immediate.rationale: German inflation surprise modestly reinforces euro-area higher-for-longer risk.

next_session.rationale: Broader euro-area drivers dilute the German-only signal.

1h.rationale: German inflation can spill into euro rates expectations.

4h.rationale: Broader index exposure and absorption reduce directional edge.

predictions.counter_case: Falling energy prices or softer euro-area data could offset the German inflation impulse.
